slots.argument: One 24-hour ticket covers the Colosseum, the Forum and the Palatine — which is why they are one morning, not three visits.
slots.shot: The Colosseum seen from above/across the Forum, whole building in frame, blue hour or hard daylight. No crowd in the foreground.

slots.argument: Free to enter, and no ticket in existence skips this. The queue is security, and security cannot be bought — only out-scheduled.
slots.shot: The security queue snaking across the cobbles toward the colonnade, shot from behind/above so no face is identifiable. The LENGTH is the subject.

slots.argument: The upgrade puts you on the arena floor, above this. What the three tickets actually buy.
slots.shot: The exposed hypogeum — cells, corridors, lift shafts — ideally with the reconstructed deck visible. Looking down into it.

slots.argument: The historic centre is two miles across. The whole trip fits inside one kilometre.
slots.shot: Rome from above at golden hour, domes and rooftops receding, the centre legible as a single compact mass.

slots.argument: Ninety seconds' walk from the monument is a different city, and a different bill.
slots.shot: A quiet Roman side street with a small trattoria — handwritten menu, no photo boards, no touts. Empty of people if possible.

slots.argument: Charm and evenings — with a bridge between you and most mornings.
slots.shot: Trastevere's cobbled lanes at dusk, ivy and shuttered windows, warm light. The mood is the argument.
